## September executive summary

- **1,336 unique human users** generated **32,114 queries**.
- Gross count was **1,338 users**; two explicitly labeled test accounts (`ci-smoke`, `test_id`) and their 36 queries were excluded.
- MAU grew **3.4% MoM**, while queries grew **8.7%**. Engagement depth grew faster than audience reach.
- Business-weighted DAU was **423**, or **441** after also excluding the apparent September 7 holiday closure.
- Rolling WAU averaged **914**, equivalent to **68.4% of MAU**.
- August-to-September retention was **82.1%**; **231 users lapsed**, while 227 new and 48 reacquired users produced net growth of 44.

## Activity distribution

Activity means at least one query. I used Pacific-local dates, weekday weight 1.0, Saturday 0.25, and Sunday 0.

| September metric | P50 | P95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Business-weighted DAU | 458 | 520 |
| Rolling seven-day WAU | 913 | 973 |
| Queries per user | 13 | 80 |
| Active days per user | 6 | 18 |
| Distinct products per user | 7 | 22 |

September 7 recorded only 20 active users versus roughly 400–530 on normal weekdays. Treating it as a closure changes weighted mean DAU from 423 to 441 but barely changes P50/P95, so the percentile findings are robust.

## Month-over-month trend

April is partial, beginning April 7.

| Month | Weighted DAU | Rolling WAU | MAU | Queries | Queries/user |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Apr | 91 | 173 | 404 | 6,308 | 15.6 |
| May | 158 | 335 | 562 | 10,573 | 18.8 |
| Jun | 213 | 460 | 724 | 13,515 | 18.7 |
| Jul | 329 | 666 | 1,107 | 24,810 | 22.4 |
| Aug | 407 | 883 | 1,292 | 29,537 | 22.9 |
| **Sep** | **423** | **914** | **1,336** | **32,114** | **24.0** |
| **Sep MoM** | **+3.8%** | **+3.5%** | **+3.4%** | **+8.7%** | **+5.1%** |

The product is still growing, but reach growth slowed materially after July and August. September growth came primarily from existing users using the product more frequently.

## Churn and reacquisition

September’s active population comprised:

- **1,061 retained from August:** 79.4% of September MAU
- **227 first-time users:** 17.0%
- **48 reacquired users:** 3.6%

Of August’s 1,292 users, **231 were inactive in September**, a monthly lapse rate of **17.9%**. The 48 reacquired users represent **11.8%** of the 408 previously seen users who were inactive in August.

This measures monthly inactivity, not confirmed account churn. True September churn cannot be determined until October data is available.

## Engagement findings

- **16.2%** of September users appeared on only one day.
- **34.2%** used the product on at least 10 days; only 10 users used it on 20 or more days.
- The top 10% of users generated **36.3% of queries**, showing meaningful but not extreme concentration.
- Median session depth was **one query**; mean was 1.8. This could indicate efficient one-shot resolution, but also limited follow-up exploration.
- Median response time was **11 seconds**, with P95 at **25 seconds**. Retry incidence was only **0.08%**.
- Feedback coverage was just **0.21%**. The 61 positive and two negative ratings are too sparse to infer overall answer quality.

## Recommended focus

1. **Prioritize second-use activation.** Target the 216 one-day users with contextual onboarding or follow-up reminders.
2. **Run a lapsed-user recovery program.** The 48 reacquisitions demonstrate recoverability; analyze the 231 August users who disappeared.
3. **Grow session depth carefully.** Test suggested follow-up questions and retained conversational context, while guarding response time and resolution quality.
4. **Plan for roughly 520 DAU at peak.** Tuesday was the busiest weekday, averaging approximately 486 active users.
5. **Improve outcome measurement.** Capture passive resolution signals or selectively request feedback; the current feedback sample is statistically inadequate.
6. **Add an eligible-user roster.** Without the total CSR population, adoption penetration and true non-user opportunity cannot be measured.
